search_log: Searched "The Last Hurrah" "Edwin O'Connor" with excerpt, first-chapter, point-of-view, third-person, narrator, and Internet Archive terms.
Opened the EBSCO Research Starter and found an explicit whole-book third-person description plus the four-part structure and Adam focalization.
Opened the eNotes character analysis and found an independent explicit description of third-person narration through Adam's perspective.
Checked the University of Chicago Press book page; its publisher description was useful for title verification but did not explicitly identify grammatical person.
Checked Google Books and Open Library previews; the accessible pages supplied bibliographic or catalog information but no usable sustained prose excerpt.
A third-party full-text page surfaced in search, but it was not relied upon because its authorization and provenance were unclear.
Targeted searches for epistolary, frame, multiple-narrator, and alternating-POV structure found no credible evidence of sustained narration in another person.
person_note: The diagnostic event passages repeatedly use sustained third-person scene narration and disclose the thoughts or perceptions of Skeffington and Adam without introducing a participating narrator. The many first-person forms occur in speeches, conversations, or embedded anecdotes and therefore do not conflict. EBSCO's whole-book structural account explicitly confirms third-person narration, usually focalized through Adam, and eNotes independently corroborates it. No credible source indicates a first-person frame or sustained alternation; the main limitation is that no authorized sustained excerpt was accessible, but the strong quote evidence and Tier B structural description independently agree.
